what_happened: During 'athena land --pr' for job w4cj, a call to GitHub (gh repos/doodla/athena) returned a transient HTTP 500. Athena did not retry and failed, so the operator had to rerun the command by hand. Bounded retry of 5xx responses was added afterward in job 86p4.
cause: Athena's external-call paths treated every failed GitHub response as final. Nothing in the design separated transient failures (5xx, network blips) from permanent ones (4xx, auth), and there was no shared retry policy for outbound calls. Each command, such as land --pr, handled errors on its own, so a flaky dependency could stop a job that was otherwise fine.
prevention: Send all outbound calls to GitHub and other external services through one wrapper. It classifies errors as transient (5xx, timeouts, connection resets) or permanent (4xx). Transient errors get bounded retries with backoff and jitter, and permanent errors fail immediately. Add a check, such as a lint or test, that fails if any command calls gh or an HTTP client directly without the wrapper. Add tests that inject a 500 for each command, land --pr included, and assert it retries and then succeeds or fails with a clear message after the limit.
proposed_request: Audit every place Athena calls GitHub (gh CLI or the API) or another external service, and route all of them through a single wrapper with bounded retry. The wrapper retries transient failures (HTTP 5xx, timeouts, connection resets) up to 3 times with exponential backoff and jitter, fails immediately on 4xx and auth errors, and logs each retry with the command name and status. Build on the 5xx retry added in job 86p4 rather than duplicating it. Add a check, as a lint rule or test, that fails when code calls gh or an HTTP client outside the wrapper. Add tests that inject a transient 500 into 'athena land --pr' and the other GitHub-calling commands. Each test should assert that a one-off 500 is retried and succeeds, and that persistent 500s fail after the limit with a clear error.
